verses.1: And when all the kings of the Amorites heard this, who lived beyond the Jordan, and all the kings of the Canaanites who lived on the sea, that Jehovah had made the waters of the Jordan stand against the Israelites until they crossed over, their hearts were filled with fear. There was no longer any hope for them from the Israelites.
verses.2: At that time, the LORD said to Joshua, “Make for yourself a plan to destroy the Canaanites. Then you can bring back the children of Israel from there again.”
verses.3: And Joshua did what was necessary to destroy the Canaanites. He ordered the children of Israel to go into the land of the Canaanites.
verses.4: And this is what Jehosua said about all those people who came out of Egypt. He mentioned all those soldiers who died on the shore, as they were leaving Egypt.
verses.5: For all the people who came out of Egypt, and all those who lived in the desert, when they left Egypt, they did not speak any language at all.
verses.6: For forty years, the children of Israel wandered in the desert until they reached the end of all those nations. These were people who had left Egypt. They did not hear the voice of Jehovah. Jehovah blessed them, but they did not see the land that He had promised to their ancestors. So they received only land covered with milk and honey.
verses.7: And he set them under his rule, just as Jehovahoshua did. They were rebellious, because he did not rule over them properly.
verses.8: And when all the people had died, they sat down in the camp until their deaths.
verses.9: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I will reveal the punishment that befell Egypt from above you.” He also named that place “Gilgal” until today.
verses.10: And the Israelites camped in Gilgal. They celebrated Passover after fourteen days, on the evenings of Yericho.
verses.11: And they ate from the fruits of the earth, starting from the day after Passover. They ate grapes and other sweet fruits on that day.
verses.12: And the clay would remain in its state after eating, from the land itself. And it was not yet time for the children of Israel to eat clay again. They ate from the produce of the land of Canaan during that year.
verses.13: And it happened that Joshua was in Jericho. He looked around, and he saw a man standing opposite him, with an axe in his hand. Joshua went up to him and said, “Peace be with you. Are you one of our enemies?”
verses.14: And he said, “Do not say that I am the king of God’s army. Now I have come here. Jehoshaphat fell before him. He bowed down and said to him, ‘What do you want, my lord? Speak to your servant.’”
verses.15: And the commander of the army of Jehovah said to Joshua, “Set your feet on that place, for it is a holy place. And Joshua did as it was commanded him.”
